content:
maya: Heads up — customer hit a crash using our JS SDK in Cloudflare Workers: `ReferenceError: require is not defined` and also `Buffer is not defined`. They import like `import {Client} from '@redwood/inference'` and it fails at bundle/runtime.
jon: can you paste the minimal repro? :eyes: 
maya: repro attached inline — worker entry:
```js
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  const client = createClient({ apiKey: '__KEY__' })
  event.respondWith(new Response('ok'))
})
```
The stack points to our transport that uses `require('buffer')` and `process.env` checks.
kevin: yeah that pattern breaks in ESM-only worker runtimes. CF workers have no Node builtins (no fs, net, Buffer, process). We need a worker-safe entrypoint or conditional exports.
sasha: we already have a `bundler` field for browser but not for edge. We should add an `exports` map that points to an ESM edge build: "./edge": "dist/edge/index.js" and doc a `type: "module"` edge build.
jon: typings are also messy — our types import `NodeJS.ReadableStream` in a couple places which drags in `lib.node`. TS users on workers have to use `tsconfig.lib: ["dom"]` which then errors on those types. We need separate `index.d.ts` for the edge entry or conditional types.
maya: other runtime quirks: AbortSignal timeout implementation differs, and `crypto.subtle` exists but not `crypto.randomBytes`. Our auth code still calls `randomBytes(16)` in refresh token routine. That's the Buffer/crypto source of the Buffer error.
kevin: simple fix: replace `randomBytes` usage with `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))` behind an env-detect helper. Also avoid `Buffer.from` by using `Uint8Array` and `TextEncoder/Decoder`.
sasha: agree. For fetch transport we should prefer `globalThis.fetch` if available, fallback to node fetch. Also expose a tiny `edge-shim.ts` that exports `createEdgeClient` and only uses web APIs. Put it under `dist/edge` and add `pkg.exports["./edge"]`.
jon: CI notes — we should add a smoke test using Miniflare in our repo to run the edge bundle (simple import + instantiate) to catch regressions. CI bot can run Miniflare in a matrix job.
ci-bot: Created pipeline job `edge-smoke-miniflare` (queued).
maya: temporary workaround for customers: use the CJS package via bundler that shims Buffer (esbuild define: globalThis.Buffer = Uint8Array?). But that's fragile.
kevin: I'll own a short PR: - add edge ESM build - add conditional exports - swap randomBytes -> getRandomValues - add edge typings file - add miniflare test. Assigning to me.
kevin: ETA EOD tomorrow for a first pass, will post a prototype.
sasha: also update README quickstart to call `import { createEdgeClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` and note environment constraints.
maya: thanks. tagging followups: add a short customer note and a remediation script snippet.
jon: can we also detect bundlers that polyfill `process.env` and warn at runtime? maybe a console.warn if process exists in worker environment.
kevin: good idea, will add a dev warning guarded by `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`. Careful to not reference `process` directly in edge bundle. Use `typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env`.
maya: cool. I'll draft a support reply with the workaround and mention upcoming edge build.
ci-bot: `edge-smoke-miniflare` job started — 1/3 steps complete.
kevin: assigning GH issue #4128 and label `edge-sdk` — will link PR shortly.
sasha: :thumbsup:
jon: thanks team.
